q: The duties of universal obligation are five and the virtues wherewith they are practiced are three.

s: the five universal duties include sovereign and minister (the duty between them)
q: The duties are those between sovereign and minister, between father and son, between husband and wife, between elder brother and younger, and those belonging to the intercourse of friends.

s: The Master teaches about government
q: The Duke Ai asked about government. The Master said, "The government of Wan and Wu is displayed in the records,—the tablets of wood and bamboo.

s: the three universal virtues is a three universally binding virtues
q: Knowledge, magnanimity, and energy, these three, are the virtues universally binding.

s: singleness is the means by which the five universal duties (they are carried into practice)
q: And the means by which they carry the duties into practice is singleness.

s: learning is near to knowledge (being fond of learning)
q: To be fond of learning is to be near to knowledge.

s: magnanimity is near to knowledge
q: To practice with vigor is to be near to magnanimity.

s: ruler follows the nine standard rules (in governing the kingdom with its states and families)
q: All who have the government of the kingdom with its states and families have nine standard rules to follow;—viz., the cultivation of their own characters; the honoring of men of virtue and talents; affection towards their relatives; respect towards the great ministers; kind and considerate treatment of the whole body of officers; dealing with the mass of the people as children; encouraging the resort of all classes of artisans; indulgent treatment of men from a distance; and the kindly cherishing of the princes of the states.

s: government depends on men (for flourishing)
q: Let there be the men and the government will flourish; but without the men, their government decays and ceases.

s: the nine standard rules are practiced by singleness
q: All who have the government of the kingdom with its states and families have the above nine standard rules. And the means by which they are carried into practice is singleness.

s: government grows rapidly with men (when the right men are present)
q: With the right men the growth of government is rapid, just as vegetation is rapid in the earth; and, moreover, their government might be called an easily-growing rush.

s: sincerity is the way of Heaven
q: Sincerity is the way of Heaven.

s: the way of men is the attainment of sincerity
q: The attainment of sincerity is the way of men.

s: sincerity is attained by the superior man (through choosing what is good and firmly holding it fast)
q: He who attains to sincerity is he who chooses what is good, and firmly holds it fast.

s: the superior man does not intermittently labor learning (until study, inquiry, reflection, discrimination, and practice are complete)
q: The superior man, while there is anything he has not studied, or while in what he has studied there is anything he cannot understand, Will not intermit his labor.

s: the superior man becomes intelligent (though dull, by persistent effort)
q: Let a man proceed in this way, and, though dull, he will surely become intelligent; though weak, he will surely become strong.

s: the superior man becomes strong (though weak, by persistent effort)
q: Let a man proceed in this way, and, though dull, he will surely become intelligent; though weak, he will surely become strong.

s: government lies in getting men (proper men)
q: Therefore the administration of government lies in getting proper men.

s: men are obtained through ruler (through the ruler's own character)
q: Such men are to be got by means of the ruler's own character.

s: ruler cultivates character and conduct (by treading in the ways of duty)
q: That character is to be cultivated by his treading in the ways of duty.

s: duty is cultivated by benevolence (through treading its ways)
q: And the treading those ways of duty is to be cultivated by the cherishing of benevolence.

s: benevolence is a characteristic element of humanity
q: Benevolence is the characteristic element of humanity, and the great exercise of it is in loving relatives.

s: the superior man embodies the course of the Mean
q: The superior man embodies the course of the Mean; the mean man acts contrary to the course of the Mean.

s: the superior man maintains the Mean (always)
q: The superior man's embodying the course of the Mean is because he is a superior man, and so always maintains the Mean.

s: mean man acts contrary to the course of the Mean
q: The superior man embodies the course of the Mean; the mean man acts contrary to the course of the Mean.

s: mean man has no caution
q: The mean man's acting contrary to the course of the Mean is because he is a mean man, and has no caution.

s: intelligence results from sincerity (when sincerity is present)
q: When we have intelligence resulting from sincerity, this condition is to be ascribed to nature;

s: intelligence is ascribed to nature (when resulting from sincerity)
q: When we have intelligence resulting from sincerity, this condition is to be ascribed to nature;

s: sincerity results from intelligence (when intelligence is present)
q: when we have sincerity resulting from intelligence, this condition is to be ascribed to instruction.

s: sincerity is ascribed to instruction (when resulting from intelligence)
q: when we have sincerity resulting from intelligence, this condition is to be ascribed to instruction.

s: intelligence is present given sincerity
q: But given the sincerity, and there shall be the intelligence;

s: sincerity is present given intelligence
q: given the intelligence, and there shall be the sincerity.

s: sincerity gives full development to nature (when possessed by a person)
q: It is only he who is possessed of the most complete sincerity that can exist under heaven, who can give its full development to his nature.

s: nature belongs to other men
q: Able to give its full development to his own nature, he can do the same to the nature of other men.

s: nature belongs to animals
q: Able to give its full development to the nature of other men, he can give their full development to the natures of animals and things.

s: nature belongs to things
q: Able to give its full development to the nature of other men, he can give their full development to the natures of animals and things.

s: sincerity assists the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth (through giving full development to the natures of creatures and things)
q: Able to give their full development to the natures of creatures and things, he can assist the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth.

s: the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth are powers of Heaven and Earth (transforming and nourishing)
q: he can assist the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth.

s: Heaven and Earth forms a ternion with a ternion (with the person possessed of the most complete sincerity)
q: Able to assist the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth, he may with Heaven and Earth form a ternion.

s: person (the cultivator of goodness) cultivates shoots of goodness (to the utmost)
q: Next to the above is he who cultivates to the utmost the shoots of goodness in him.

s: person (the cultivator of goodness) can transform what exists under heaven (only when possessed of the most complete sincerity)
q: It is only he who is possessed of the most complete sincerity that can exist under heaven, who can transform.

s: person (the cultivator of goodness) can attain sincerity (from the shoots of goodness)
q: From those he can attain to the possession of sincerity.

s: sincerity becomes apparent apparent
q: This sincerity becomes apparent.

s: sincerity becomes manifest manifest
q: From being apparent, it becomes manifest.

s: sincerity becomes brilliant brilliant
q: From being manifest, it becomes brilliant.

s: sincerity affects others
q: Brilliant, it affects others.

s: others are changed by sincerity
q: Affecting others, they are changed by it.

s: others are transformed by sincerity
q: Changed by it, they are transformed.

s: person (the cultivator of goodness) possesses sincerity (the most complete)
q: It is only he who is possessed of the most complete sincerity that can exist under heaven, who can transform.

s: sincerity can foreknow what is about to happen (as a characteristic of complete sincerity)
q: It is characteristic of the most entire sincerity to be able to foreknow.

s: individual possessed of the most complete sincerity can foreknow happiness (when it is about to come)
q: When calamity or happiness is about to come, the good shall certainly be foreknown by him, and the evil also.

s: individual possessed of the most complete sincerity can foreknow calamity (when it is about to come)
q: When calamity or happiness is about to come, the good shall certainly be foreknown by him, and the evil also.

s: individual possessed of the most complete sincerity is like spirit (as an individual possessed of the most complete sincerity)
q: Therefore the individual possessed of the most complete sincerity is like a spirit.

s: nation has happy omens (when it is about to flourish)
q: When a nation or family is about to flourish, there are sure to be happy omens;

s: family has happy omens (when it is about to flourish)
q: When a nation or family is about to flourish, there are sure to be happy omens;

s: nation has unlucky omens (when it is about to perish)
q: and when it is about to perish, there are sure to be unlucky omens.

s: family has unlucky omens (when it is about to perish)
q: and when it is about to perish, there are sure to be unlucky omens.

s: happy omens affect movements of the four limbs (as such events)
q: Such events are seen in the milfoil and tortoise, and affect the movements of the four limbs.

s: unlucky omens affect movements of the four limbs (as such events)
q: Such events are seen in the milfoil and tortoise, and affect the movements of the four limbs.

s: happy omens are seen in milfoil (as such events)
q: Such events are seen in the milfoil and tortoise, and affect the movements of the four limbs.

s: happy omens are seen in tortoise (as such events)
q: Such events are seen in the milfoil and tortoise, and affect the movements of the four limbs.

s: sincerity effects self-completion
q: Sincerity is that whereby self-completion is effected

s: knowledge is shown by other men (as the completing other men and things)
q: The completing other men and things shows his knowledge.

s: the virtue according to the Mean belongs to nature (as a virtue belonging to the nature)
q: But these are virtues belonging to the nature

s: knowledge belongs to nature (as a virtue belonging to the nature)
q: But these are virtues belonging to the nature

s: the way directs man (as the means by which man must direct himself)
q: its way is that by which man must direct himself

s: sincerity is the end of things
q: Sincerity is the end and beginning of things

s: sincerity is the beginning of things
q: Sincerity is the end and beginning of things

s: the superior man regards as most excellent sincerity (attainment of sincerity)
q: the superior man regards the attainment of sincerity as the most excellent thing

s: sincerity completes self-completion (through its possessor)
q: The possessor of sincerity does not merely accomplish the self-completion of himself.

s: sincerity completes other men (through its possessor)
q: With this quality he completes other men and things also.

s: sincerity completes things (through its possessor)
q: With this quality he completes other men and things also.

s: self-completion shows the virtue according to the Mean (as the completing himself)
q: The completing himself shows his perfect virtue.

s: sincerity has ceaselessness
q: Hence to entire sincerity there belongs ceaselessness.

s: individual possessed of the most entire sincerity is co equal with Heaven (as high and brilliant)
q: So high and brilliant, it makes him the co-equal of Heaven.

s: individual possessed of the most entire sincerity is infinite (as far-reaching and long-continuing)
q: So far-reaching and long-continuing, it makes him infinite.

s: the way of Heaven and Earth is a way
q: The way of Heaven and Earth may be completely declared in one sentence.

s: the way of Heaven and Earth is without doubleness
q: They are without any doubleness, and so they produce things in a manner that is unfathomable.

s: the way of Heaven and Earth produces things (in an unfathomable manner)
q: They are without any doubleness, and so they produce things in a manner that is unfathomable.

s: the way of Heaven and Earth is large and substantial large and substantial
q: The way of Heaven and Earth is large and substantial, high and brilliant, far-reaching and long-enduring.

s: the way of Heaven and Earth is high and brilliant high and brilliant
q: The way of Heaven and Earth is large and substantial, high and brilliant, far-reaching and long-enduring.

s: the way of Heaven and Earth is far reaching and long enduring far-reaching and long-enduring
q: The way of Heaven and Earth is large and substantial, high and brilliant, far-reaching and long-enduring.

s: Heaven contains sun (in its inexhaustible extent)
q: The Heaven now before us is only this bright shining spot; but when viewed in its inexhaustible extent, the sun, moon, stars, and constellations of the zodiac, are suspended in it, and all things are overspread by it.

s: Heaven contains moon (in its inexhaustible extent)
q: The Heaven now before us is only this bright shining spot; but when viewed in its inexhaustible extent, the sun, moon, stars, and constellations of the zodiac, are suspended in it, and all things are overspread by it.

s: ceaselessness continues long (without ceasing)
q: Not ceasing, it continues long.

s: Heaven contains stars (in its inexhaustible extent)
q: The Heaven now before us is only this bright shining spot; but when viewed in its inexhaustible extent, the sun, moon, stars, and constellations of the zodiac, are suspended in it, and all things are overspread by it.

s: Heaven contains constellations of the zodiac (in its inexhaustible extent)
q: The Heaven now before us is only this bright shining spot; but when viewed in its inexhaustible extent, the sun, moon, stars, and constellations of the zodiac, are suspended in it, and all things are overspread by it.

s: Heaven overspreads all things (in its inexhaustible extent)
q: The Heaven now before us is only this bright shining spot; but when viewed in its inexhaustible extent, the sun, moon, stars, and constellations of the zodiac, are suspended in it, and all things are overspread by it.

s: Earth sustains mountains Hwa and Yo (in its breadth and thickness)
q: The earth before us is but a handful of soil; but when regarded in its breadth and thickness, it sustains mountains like the Hwa and the Yo, without feeling their weight, and contains the rivers and seas, without their leaking away.

s: Earth contains rivers (without their leaking away)
q: The earth before us is but a handful of soil; but when regarded in its breadth and thickness, it sustains mountains like the Hwa and the Yo, without feeling their weight, and contains the rivers and seas, without their leaking away.

s: Earth contains seas (without their leaking away)
q: The earth before us is but a handful of soil; but when regarded in its breadth and thickness, it sustains mountains like the Hwa and the Yo, without feeling their weight, and contains the rivers and seas, without their leaking away.

s: ceaselessness reaches far
q: Evidencing itself, it reaches far.

s: Book of Poetry states the ordinances of Heaven are profound and unceasing
q: It is said in the Book of Poetry, "The ordinances of Heaven, how profound are they and unceasing!"

s: King Wan has singleness of virtue (illustrious and unceasing)
q: And again, "How illustrious was it, the singleness of the virtue of King Wan!" indicating that it was thus that King Wan was what he was.

s: ceaselessness is large and substantial large and substantial
q: Reaching far, it becomes large and substantial.

s: ceaselessness is high and brilliant high and brilliant
q: Large and substantial, it becomes high and brilliant.

s: ceaselessness contains all things (as large and substantial)
q: Large and substantial;—this is how it contains all things.

s: ceaselessness overspreads all things (as high and brilliant)
q: High and brilliant;—this is how it overspreads all things.

s: ceaselessness perfects all things (as far-reaching and long-continuing)
q: Reaching far and continuing long;—this is how it perfects all things.

s: individual possessed of the most entire sincerity is co equal with Earth (as large and substantial)
q: So large and substantial, the individual possessing it is the co-equal of Earth.

s: the way of the superior man is a path
q: How great is the path proper to the Sage!

s: the superior man honors his virtuous nature
q: Therefore, the superior man honors his virtuous nature, and maintains constant inquiry and study, seeking to carry it out to its breadth and greatness, so as to omit none of the more exquisite and minute points which it embraces, and to raise it to its greatest height and brilliancy, so as to pursue the course of the Mean.

s: the superior man honors virtuous nature (the superior man's)
q: Therefore, the superior man honors his virtuous nature, and maintains constant inquiry and study, seeking to carry it out to its breadth and greatness, so as to omit none of the more exquisite and minute points which it embraces, and to raise it to its greatest height and brilliancy, so as to pursue the course of the Mean.

s: the superior man maintains constant inquiry and study
q: Therefore, the superior man honors his virtuous nature, and maintains constant inquiry and study, seeking to carry it out to its breadth and greatness, so as to omit none of the more exquisite and minute points which it embraces, and to raise it to its greatest height and brilliancy, so as to pursue the course of the Mean.

s: the superior man pursues the Mean (by raising virtuous nature to its greatest height and brilliancy)
q: Therefore, the superior man honors his virtuous nature, and maintains constant inquiry and study, seeking to carry it out to its breadth and greatness, so as to omit none of the more exquisite and minute points which it embraces, and to raise it to its greatest height and brilliancy, so as to pursue the course of the Mean.

s: the superior man cherishes old knowledge
q: He cherishes his old knowledge, and is continually acquiring new.

s: the superior man acquires new knowledge (continually)
q: He cherishes his old knowledge, and is continually acquiring new.

s: the superior man practices propriety (with honest, generous earnestness)
q: He exerts an honest, generous earnestness, in the esteem and practice of all propriety.

s: the superior man is not proud proud (when occupying a high situation)
q: Thus, when occupying a high situation he is not proud, and in a low situation he is not insubordinate.

s: the superior man is not insubordinate insubordinate (when in a low situation)
q: Thus, when occupying a high situation he is not proud, and in a low situation he is not insubordinate.

s: kingdom is well governed well governed
q: When the kingdom is well governed, he is sure by his words to rise;

s: the way of the superior man resembles overflowing water (in its abundance)
q: Like overflowing water, it sends forth and nourishes all things, and rises up to the height of heaven.

s: the superior man rises by his words (when the kingdom is well governed)
q: When the kingdom is well governed, he is sure by his words to rise;

s: kingdom is ill governed ill governed
q: and when it is ill governed, he is sure by his silence to command forbearance to himself.

s: the superior man commands forbearance to himself (by his silence when the kingdom is ill governed)
q: and when it is ill governed, he is sure by his silence to command forbearance to himself.

s: the superior man is intelligent intelligent
q: Intelligent is he and prudent, and so preserves his person?

s: the superior man is prudent prudent
q: Intelligent is he and prudent, and so preserves his person?

s: Book of Poetry contains the statement that the superior man is intelligent and prudent
q: Is not this what we find in the Book of Poetry,—"Intelligent is he and prudent, and so preserves his person?"

s: the way of the superior man nourishes all things
q: Like overflowing water, it sends forth and nourishes all things, and rises up to the height of heaven.

s: the way of the superior man rises to height of heaven
q: Like overflowing water, it sends forth and nourishes all things, and rises up to the height of heaven.

s: the way of the superior man is complete all-complete
q: All-complete is its greatness!

s: the way of the superior man embraces the three hundred rules of ceremony
q: It embraces the three hundred rules of ceremony, and the three thousand rules of demeanor.

s: the way of the superior man embraces the three thousand rules of demeanor
q: It embraces the three hundred rules of ceremony, and the three thousand rules of demeanor.

s: the way of the superior man waits for proper man
q: It waits for the proper man, and then it is trodden.

s: the way of the superior man is made a fact by perfect virtue (in all its courses)
q: Only by perfect virtue can the perfect path, in all its courses, be made a fact.

s: kingdom has writing (throughout)
q: Now over the kingdom, carriages have all wheels, of the-same size; all writing is with the same characters;

s: kingdom has rules (for conduct)
q: and for conduct there are the same rules.

s: throne may be occupied without proper virtue (but the occupant may not make ceremonies or music)
q: One may occupy the throne, but if he have not the proper virtue, he may not dare to make ceremonies or music.

s: virtue may exist without throne (but its possessor may not presume to make ceremonies or music)
q: One may have the virtue, but if he do not occupy the throne, he may not presume to make ceremonies or music.

s: The Master may describe ceremonies of the Hsia dynasty (but Chi cannot sufficiently attest his words)
q: I may describe the ceremonies of the Hsia dynasty, but Chi cannot sufficiently attest my words.

s: The Master has learned ceremonies of the Yin dynasty
q: I have learned the ceremonies of the Yin dynasty,

s: The Master has learned ceremonies of Chau
q: I have learned the ceremonies of Chau, which are now used,

s: ceremonies of Chau are used now
q: I have learned the ceremonies of Chau, which are now used,

s: The Master follows Chau (in ceremonies)
q: and I follow Chau.

s: Son of Heaven orders ceremonies (exclusively)
q: To no one but the Son of Heaven does it belong to order ceremonies,

s: Son of Heaven fixes measures (exclusively)
q: To no one but the Son of Heaven does it belong to order ceremonies, to fix the measures,

s: Son of Heaven determines written characters (exclusively)
q: To no one but the Son of Heaven does it belong to order ceremonies, to fix the measures, and to determine the written characters.

s: kingdom has carriages (throughout)
q: Now over the kingdom, carriages have all wheels, of the-same size;

s: Ruler is a sovereign (of the kingdom)
q: He who attains to the sovereignty of the kingdom, having those three important things, shall be able to effect that there shall be few errors under his government.

s: kingdom receives law (from the Ruler's acts for ages)
q: His acts are for ages a law to the kingdom.

s: kingdom receives lesson (from the Ruler's words for ages)
q: His words are for ages a lesson to the kingdom.

s: regulations is a former institutions (when made by those of former times)
q: However excellent may have been the regulations of those of former times, they cannot be attested.

s: regulations cannot be attested unattested (when belonging to former times)
q: However excellent may have been the regulations of those of former times, they cannot be attested.

s: regulations cannot command credence (when not attested)
q: Not being attested, they cannot command credence, and not being credited, the people would not follow them.

s: people follows regulations (only when credited)
q: Not being attested, they cannot command credence, and not being credited, the people would not follow them.

s: institutions is rooted in character and conduct (of the Ruler)
q: Therefore the institutions of the Ruler are rooted in his own character and conduct, and sufficient attestation of them is given by the masses of the people.

s: institutions is attested by people (sufficiently, through the masses of the people)
q: Therefore the institutions of the Ruler are rooted in his own character and conduct, and sufficient attestation of them is given by the masses of the people.

s: Ruler has institutions (as the basis of government)
q: Therefore the institutions of the Ruler are rooted in his own character and conduct, and sufficient attestation of them is given by the masses of the people.

s: institutions conforms to Heaven (without anything contrary to its mode of operation)
q: He sets them up before Heaven and Earth, and finds nothing in them contrary to their mode of operation.

s: institutions conforms to Earth (without anything contrary to its mode of operation)
q: He sets them up before Heaven and Earth, and finds nothing in them contrary to their mode of operation.

s: institutions is accepted by spiritual beings (without doubts arising)
q: He presents himself with them before spiritual beings, and no doubts about them arise.

s: Heaven has mode of operation (shared with Earth)
q: He sets them up before Heaven and Earth, and finds nothing in them contrary to their mode of operation.

s: Earth has mode of operation (shared with Heaven)
q: He sets them up before Heaven and Earth, and finds nothing in them contrary to their mode of operation.

s: spiritual beings have no doubts (about the Ruler's institutions)
q: He presents himself with them before spiritual beings, and no doubts about them arise.

s: world receives example (from the Ruler's movements for ages)
q: Such being the case, the movements of such a ruler, illustrating his institutions, constitute an example to the world for ages.

s: those who are far from the Ruler looks longingly for Ruler (because of his enduring example)
q: Those who are far from him look longingly for him; and those who are near him are never wearied with him.

s: Ruler is compared with three kings (to test his institutions for mistakes)
q: He examines them by comparison with those of the three kings, and finds them without mistake.

s: those who are near the Ruler is not weary of Ruler (through continued proximity)
q: Those who are far from him look longingly for him; and those who are near him are never wearied with him.

s: Book of Poetry contains description (of a ruler's enduring praise)
